title: Though in the Midst of Life We Be
description: Though in the Midst of Life We Be in Tonic Solfa: the solfa line by line with the words, staff notation, all 3 verses, and a piano to sing along with.
about: The words are by Martin Luther, first published in 1524. The English translation is by Richard Massie (1854). The tune, MITTEN WIR IM LEBEN SIND, is by Martin Luther (1524). This version of the melody and the words comes from the Open Hymnal Project.
underlay: Though in midst of life we be,_ Snares of death sur-round__ us; Where shall we for suc-cor flee,_ Lest our foes con-found__ us? To Thee a-lone, our Sa_-vior. We mourn our grie-vous sin which hath_ Stirr'd the fire of Thy_ fierce wrath. Ho-ly and gra-cious God! Ho-ly and might-y God! Ho-ly and all‑ mer-ci-ful Sa_-vior! Thou e-ter-nal God! Save us, Lord, from sink_-ing In the deep and bit-ter flood. Ky-ri-e e-lei-son.

lines: Though in midst of life we be,
Where shall we for succor flee,
We mourn our grievous sin which hath
Stirr'd the fire of Thy fierce wrath.
In the deep and bitter flood.
Whilst in midst of death we be,
Who from such distress will free.
Thou only, Lord, canst do it!
It moves Thy tender heart to see
With its deep and burning flood.
Where shall we for succor flee,
Who, O, who will hide us?
Thy precious blood was shed to win
Peace and pardon for our sin.
Fall in our last need away.
